analyst_view.overall: Mid-table neighbours one point apart: Córdoba (10th, 20 points) are unbeaten in five league games after a 3-3 at Mallorca and are strong at El Arcángel, while Oviedo (9th, 21 points) have only 8 points at home but 13 away, and lost 1-2 to Girona in Raúl González's debut after Julián Calero was sacked; Mikel Goti has taken over from Jacobo González up front. Córdoba's Cristian Carracedo has a myofascial injury in his left leg (confirmed 17 November) and missed the Mallorca game; his availability is left to the medical staff, and Medina, Diarra, Fomeyem and Jacobo Martí are also out. Oviedo still miss Dani Calvo and Chris Ramos, which the numbers already count. Cordópolis notes these are the two most booked sides in Segunda (Córdoba 48 yellows, Oviedo 45), with four Córdoba players a yellow away from a ban; no referee is named yet.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals, a high total for two open sides, and already adjust for Calvo and Ramos. Carracedo, Córdoba's main creator, is still unconfirmed with a leg injury the numbers don't know about, though El Jebari scored in his place at Mallorca, so I keep only a small trim, to about 3.0.

corners.text: The numbers say 11.5 corners, 7.3 of them Córdoba's, and already add 12% for Córdoba's recent run of corners at home. Raúl's direct Oviedo could create more transitions, but that does not clearly change corner counts, so I stay at 11.5.

cards.text: The numbers say 6.3 cards, already high because these are the two most booked teams in the league and their recent bookings are counted (+10% and +9%). Four Córdoba players on four yellows might hold back a little, while a new coach asking for pressing can mean more fouls; with no referee named, I stay at 6.3.

shots.text: The numbers say 31.9 shots, a very open game, with both sides' recent high shot counts already adding about 12%. Córdoba's second-half dips and both benches' habit of changing games are in their records, so I stay at about 32.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.5 shots on target. If Carracedo misses out, Córdoba lose their best supplier of chances, so I trim slightly to about 10.3, keeping it small because his status is unclear.
